slides.texte_overlay:
Skills that will make you
impossible to ignore
Learn to speak up early in meetings. Not loud, just early. "Can I throw out one idea?" The first decent idea in the room usually sets the direction, and everyone remembers who said it.

Learn to hold eye contact one second longer. When you finish a sentence, don't look away straight away. Stay there, relaxed. It sounds tiny. It's the difference between sounding unsure and sounding like you mean it.
Learn to keep your voice low and slow. When you're nervous, you talk faster and higher. Slow down, finish your sentences, let a pause sit. People lean in to listen to someone who isn't rushing.
Become the guy who can talk about anything. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. Like why the Mona Lisa only got famous after it was stolen. Range is rare, and people notice it fast.
slides.texte_sophia: Become the guy who can talk about anything. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Range is rare, and people notice it fast.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn to finish what you start. The course, the side project, the half-built shelf. Most people quit at eighty percent. Show up with the finished thing and you're suddenly the most reliable guy anyone knows.
Learn to say what you want clearly. Not "I was kind of thinking maybe..." but "I'd like to lead this one." A clear ask sounds confident, and confident people are the ones who get picked.

Learn to stay calm when things go wrong. Flight cancelled, plan falls apart, someone starts panicking. Just say "Okay, here's what we do." The calm one in a crisis is the one everyone remembers afterwards.
